label: early copy phase, outputting the 3rd original token (recall_idx 2), longer sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase. It never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter, and never on a first occurrence of a token. 75% of activation mass is at recall_idx 2 (input orig(1), output orig(2)), with the rest at recall_idx 1 and 3. It is rare later in the copy. The rate rises with L (almost nothing at L<=4) and with to_go 3-6. Magnitude depends strongly on token identity. Outputting z, or z as the next output, gives about 10x lift. f and o give about 4-5x, and the top examples are recall_idx 2 steps with orig(2)=z. However, no small token set captures it: z-only predicates reach high precision but low recall. Only ~19-27% of recall_idx 2 steps are active, and which ones fire depends on the token content in a diffuse way, so precision is low.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: z, f, o, p, b, h; least: d, a, y, v) and the next token to output (most: z, o, f, p, j, 3; least: d, -, y, v); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=2, recall_idx=3, t=10.
